paragraphs: The First Sports Teacher of Our School, posted by Lily. On Thursday, Coach Matt came to the school library. He told the Explorers about the first sports teacher of our school. Her name was Hazel Brooks, and she lived many years ago. The Explorers listened, and Lily took notes. She taught outdoors, and she started the first rugby team at our school.

Hazel was born in a village near a river. As a child, she swam in the river every day. Her family had no pool, so the river was her pool. She taught herself to dive from a low bank. Nobody showed her how, so she watched the older children who swam. She learned fast, and her diving was very good. People came to the river to watch her.

At the age of eighteen, she took a test to become a teacher. The test was hard, and she studied at night. She passed it, and she came to our school as the first sports teacher. Many people in the village were proud of her. The school had no gym, so she taught outdoors. She used the field and the space near the gate as her classroom. Sometimes she took the children to a pool near the river.

One day, a visitor gave her an old book about rugby. She learned the game herself, and then she taught it to the children. She made two wooden posts for the field with her own hands. The first team had only eight children. The children laughed, and they fell down many times. She said, "Fall, stand up, and try again." The ball was too big for them, so she found a smaller ball at the market.

After one year, the school had a rugby team with twenty children. She started the first training day for girls and boys together. The first game was on a hot afternoon. People from the town came to watch the first game. Her wooden posts stood on the field for many years. "Today, our school still has a rugby team because of her," said Coach Matt. He also showed us an old photo of the wooden posts.
Then Leo asked, "Can girls play rugby today?" "Yes, of course," said Coach Matt. "Many girls play in our school team." Lily wrote the story down in her notebook. She wants to learn a new sport too.
